inputs.abstract:
The classes NP and PTIME of the descriptive-complexity library, which are
defined by logics on finite structures, are the textbook classes on bit strings.
Over a vocabulary with finitely many relation symbols, a decision problem is in
NP exactly when the language of the binary encodings of its yes-instances has
polynomially bounded certificates checked in polynomial time by a Mathlib
Turing machine (FinTM2); it is in PTIME exactly when such a machine decides that
language in polynomial time. The encodings and the machine classes are those of
Szymon Toruńczyk's lax-988886 (Fagin's theorem) and lax-751879 (the
Immerman–Vardi theorem), required here, and each machine statement is one
application of a registered capture theorem.

The content of this submission is the logical side, which assumes neither
theorem: the library's second-order definition of NP agrees with the existential
second-order logic of lax-988886, and the library's definition of PTIME with the
FO(LFP) of lax-751879. The second agreement carries the proofs. Going to the
archive's syntax turns one simultaneous least fixed point into nested ones, by
Bekić's principle. Coming back turns nested, negated, and parameterized fixed
points into one inflationary induction, by a construction that iterates a program
in a relation it reads, its rounds being the tuples of the universe, each round
starting from empty relations and opening once the previous round has converged.

concepts.title: NP and PTIME against the logics of the two entries
concepts.description:
A decision problem is in NP exactly when it reads as a property defined by an existential
second-order sentence of the Fagin entry, and in PTIME exactly when it reads as a query
defined by an FO(LFP) formula of the Immerman–Vardi entry. Neither statement mentions a
machine, and neither proof assumes a capture theorem. The second is the substance of this
submission: the formulas of the entry may nest, negate, and parameterize their fixed points,
whereas the definitions of the library have one simultaneous fixed point.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax832283.StringProblems
import Lax904597.Classes
import Lax535992.ClassPTIME
import Lax751879.FixedPointSemantics
import Lax988886.ExistentialSecondOrder

/-!
---
title: NP and PTIME against the logics of the two entries
type: theorem
---
A decision problem is in NP exactly when it reads as a property defined by an existential
second-order sentence of the Fagin entry, and in PTIME exactly when it reads as a query
defined by an FO(LFP) formula of the Immerman–Vardi entry. Neither statement mentions a
machine, and neither proof assumes a capture theorem. The second is the substance of this
submission: the formulas of the entry may nest, negate, and parameterize their fixed points,
whereas the definitions of the library have one simultaneous fixed point.
-/

namespace Lax832283.LogicalBridge

open FirstOrder Lax904597.Problems Lax904597.Classes Lax535992.ClassPTIME
open Lax832283.StringProblems

/-- NP, against the existential second-order logic of the Fagin entry. -/
axiom mem_NP_iff_definable {L : Language.{0, 0}} [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L)
    (P : DecisionProblem L) :
    NP.Mem P ↔ Lax988886.ExistentialSecondOrder.Definable (toProperty V P)

/-- PTIME, against the FO(LFP) of the Immerman–Vardi entry. -/
axiom mem_PTIME_iff_definable {L : Language.{0, 0}} [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L)
    (P : DecisionProblem L) :
    PTIME.Mem P ↔ Lax751879.FixedPointSemantics.Definable (toQuery V P)

end Lax832283.LogicalBridge

concepts.title: NP and PTIME are the textbook classes on bit strings
concepts.description:
A decision problem is in NP exactly when the language of the binary encodings of its
yes-instances has polynomially bounded certificates checked by a polynomial-time Mathlib
machine, and in PTIME exactly when a polynomial-time Mathlib machine decides that language.
The encodings of the yes-instances of SAT and of HORN-SAT are examples, for any numbering of
their vocabulary.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax832283.LogicalBridge
import Lax904597.CookLevin
import Lax535992.HornSatPTIMEComplete
import Lax751879.ImmermanVardi
import Lax988886.Fagin

/-!
---
title: NP and PTIME are the textbook classes on bit strings
type: theorem
---
A decision problem is in NP exactly when the language of the binary encodings of its
yes-instances has polynomially bounded certificates checked by a polynomial-time Mathlib
machine, and in PTIME exactly when a polynomial-time Mathlib machine decides that language.
The encodings of the yes-instances of SAT and of HORN-SAT are examples, for any numbering of
their vocabulary.
-/

namespace Lax832283.MachineBridge

open FirstOrder Lax904597.Problems Lax904597.Classes Lax535992.ClassPTIME
open Lax832283.StringProblems Lax988886.FiniteStructures
open Lax988886.NondeterministicPolynomialTime Lax751879.PolynomialTime

/-- NP is the textbook class. -/
axiom mem_NP_iff_inNP {L : Language.{0, 0}} [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L)
    (P : DecisionProblem L) : NP.Mem P ↔ InNP (toProperty V P)

/-- NP, on bit strings. -/
axiom mem_NP_iff_languageInNP {L : Language.{0, 0}} [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L)
    (P : DecisionProblem L) :
    NP.Mem P ↔ LanguageInNP (Lax988886.FiniteStructures.language (toProperty V P))

/-- PTIME is the textbook class. -/
axiom mem_PTIME_iff_inP {L : Language.{0, 0}} [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L)
    (P : DecisionProblem L) : PTIME.Mem P ↔ InP (toQuery V P)

/-- The encodings of satisfiable CNF instances form a language in NP. -/
axiom SAT_languageInNP (V : FinVocab Lax904597.Sat.sat) :
    LanguageInNP (Lax988886.FiniteStructures.language (toProperty V Lax904597.Sat.SAT))

/-- A polynomial-time machine decides the encodings of the satisfiable Horn instances. -/
axiom HORNSAT_inP (V : FinVocab Lax904597.Sat.sat) :
    InP (toQuery V Lax535992.HornSat.HORNSAT)

end Lax832283.MachineBridge

concepts.title: Decision problems of the core on bit strings
concepts.description:
A vocabulary of the NP core, with finitely many relation symbols, is numbered by a
list of arities. A table of the Immerman–Vardi entry, of that list of arities, then reads
as a structure on an initial segment of the natural numbers, and a decision problem of
the core reads as a property of tables and as a Boolean query. The empty table is a
no-instance, the classes of the core being about nonempty structures. A word that encodes
no table is in no language of the two entries, so nothing else needs care.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Syntax
import Mathlib.Data.Fin.Tuple.Basic
import Mathlib.Logic.Equiv.Fin.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.List.OfFn
import Mathlib.Data.Finite.Card
import Mathlib.Algebra.BigOperators.Group.List.Basic
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Nat.Defs
import Mathlib.Algebra.Group.Action.Defs
import Mathlib.Data.List.FinRange
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Semantics
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Complexity
import Mathlib.Tactic.FinCases
import Lax751879.OrderedStructures
import Lax904597.Problems
import Lax988886.FiniteStructures

/-!
---
title: Decision problems of the core on bit strings
type: definition
---
A vocabulary of the NP core, with finitely many relation symbols, is numbered by a
list of arities. A table of the Immerman–Vardi entry, of that list of arities, then reads
as a structure on an initial segment of the natural numbers, and a decision problem of
the core reads as a property of tables and as a Boolean query. The empty table is a
no-instance, the classes of the core being about nonempty structures. A word that encodes
no table is in no language of the two entries, so nothing else needs care.
-/

namespace Lax832283.StringProblems

open Lax751879.OrderedStructures Lax904597.Problems Lax988886.FiniteStructures

open FirstOrder

/-- An enumeration of the relation symbols of `L`, listing their arities. -/
structure FinVocab (L : Language.{0, 0}) where
  /-- The arities of the symbols, in the order of the enumeration. -/
  σ : List ℕ
  /-- The symbol of a given number, with its arity. -/
  sym : Fin σ.length ≃ Σ n, L.Relations n
  /-- The list records the arity of each symbol. -/
  arity_sym : ∀ i, (sym i).1 = σ.get i

namespace FinVocab

variable {L : Language.{0, 0}}

variable (V : FinVocab L)

/-- The number of a given symbol. -/
def toSym {n : ℕ} (R : L.Relations n) : Fin V.σ.length :=
  V.sym.symm ⟨n, R⟩

end FinVocab

open FirstOrder Language Structure



variable {L : Language.{0, 0}}

/-- Read a table of the archive's formalism as a structure of the library. -/
@[reducible]
def ofOrdered [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L) (S : OrderedStructure V.σ) :
    L.Structure (Fin S.size) where
  funMap f := isEmptyElim f
  RelMap {n} R v := S.relation (V.toSym R) (v ∘ Fin.cast
    (show V.σ.get (V.toSym R) = n by rw [← V.arity_sym, FinVocab.toSym, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]))
    = true

/-- A decision problem of the library, as a property of the archive's structures. The
empty structure is a no-instance. -/
def toProperty [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L) (P : DecisionProblem L) :
    Property V.σ :=
  fun S => 0 < S.size ∧ @DecisionProblem.Holds L _ P (Fin S.size) (ofOrdered V S)

/-- A decision problem of the library, as a Boolean query on ordered structures. -/
def toQuery [L.IsRelational] (V : FinVocab L) (P : DecisionProblem L) : Query V.σ 0 :=
  fun S => toProperty V P S.structureValue

end Lax832283.StringProblems
